name: 5/3/1 for Beginners
author: Jim Wendler
summary: A three-day full-body version of 5/3/1 where every session trains two main lifts with the 5/3/1 sets followed by 5x5 First Set Last, then push, pull and single-leg/core assistance. Weights come from a submaximal training max that rises a small, fixed amount each cycle.
evidenceNote: Squat and bench each get about 16 main-lift sets a week, deadlift and press about 8, plus 150-300 assistance reps a day, so weekly volume is solid for a beginner. Most sets stop well short of failure, with one '+' set per lift as the hard set. TM progression is deliberately slow (2.5/5 kg per cycle), which is far slower than a novice could manage on a linear program. Lifters who want maximum early strength gains may outgrow it, but it is good for building technique and work capacity.

sources.title: The 5/3/1 Philosophy for Beginners (Jim Wendler blog)
5/3/1: How to Build Pure Strength (T Nation interview with Jim Wendler)
5/3/1 for Beginners (The Fitness Wiki, community summary of the Wendler article)

schedule: Monday, Wednesday, Friday full body: Mon squat + bench, Wed deadlift + press, Fri bench + squat. Off days (Tue/Thu/Sat/Sun): running or conditioning following the 5/3/1 '50% rule'. Before lifting do DeFranco's Agile 8 and 10-15 total box jumps or med-ball throws.

progression.description: Training max (TM): the beginner article says to take 80-85% of your max and work up slowly, erring on the side of too light; this template uses 85%. (Wendler's TM calculator labels 85% 'recommended for most' and 90% 'beginner'; the original T Nation 5/3/1 used 90%.) All percentages are of the TM. The beginner article does not list the weekly percentages; they come from the original 5/3/1 (T Nation): week 1 65/75/85% x5/5/5+, week 2 70/80/90% x3/3/3+, week 3 75/85/95% x5/3/1+. Each main lift is followed by 5x5 at that day's first-set percentage (First Set Last). After each cycle add 5 lb (2.5 kg) to the TM for bench and press and 10 lb (5 kg) for squat and deadlift (the original T Nation article adds these amounts to the max and recalculates; The Fitness Wiki applies them to the TM after every 3-week cycle). Every rep must be fast with good form; if any rep in the cycle was slow, grinding or broke form, do not increase that TM.
progression.deload: Not specified in the free beginner article. The Fitness Wiki summary runs 3-week cycles back to back (with an optional TM test week after three cycles, which it notes is not in the original article). Week 4 here is the original 5/3/1 deload (40/50/60% x5, T Nation) and is marked optional. Missed or poor-quality reps mean the TM is not increased.

exercises.notes: 5/3/1 sets; last set is the '+' set (as many good reps as possible).

exercises.name: Squat - First Set Last (FSL)
exercises.notes: 5x5 at the first-set percentage of the day (65% TM).

exercises.name: Push assistance
exercises.notes: Author: one exercise per category per day, 50-100 total reps in any number of sets; add a second movement if you cannot reach the reps. Options: dips, push-ups, DB bench/incline/press, triceps extensions/pushdowns.

exercises.name: Pull assistance
exercises.notes: Author: one exercise per category per day, 50-100 total reps in any number of sets; add a second movement if you cannot reach the reps. Options: chin-ups/pull-ups, inverted rows, DB/machine/BB rows, face pulls, band pull-aparts, lat pulldown, curls.

notes: The beginner article gives the layout, FSL, TM range, assistance and conditioning but refers to the book for the core percentages; those come from the free T Nation article describing the original 5/3/1, and match The Fitness Wiki summary of the beginner program. Wendler's most important assistance picks: DB squats, DB rows, chins/pull-ups, push-ups, dips, back raises, ab wheel and bodyweight squats. Beginner standards he gives: 10 chin-ups or pull-ups, 35 push-ups, 20 dips, DB squat with half bodyweight for 20. Rest periods are not given. sessionMinutes is an estimate.
